title: Token spike — hiring protocol variants and pricing sensitivity notes
body:
Purpose:
To document a compact set of hiring-protocol variants and associated pricing sensitivity assumptions for short-lived and sustained token spikes. This is a working note intended to feed into the Q3 capacity playbook and the SLA contingency runbook. Not final — objective is to converge on threshold rules and quick-action templates.

Background and motivation:
- Over the last 18 months we’ve seen three distinct demand patterns: micro-bursts (minutes-hours), multi-day spikes (3–14 days), and sustained growth (weeks+).
- Current headcount gating is coarse: approvals kick in only after a 3-week projection breach. That delay risks degraded SLAs or expensive last-minute contractor sourcing.
- This doc proposes alternative "awaiting-hire" protocols that pair pricing levers with headcount actions so we can respond faster and cheaper.

Key assumptions (working):
- Baseline token throughput: 1.6B tokens/day across hosted+dedicated.
- Baseline committed capacity cushion: 18% (GPU headroom + burst credits).
- Average MLOps ramp time (contractor sourcing + onboarding): 7–21 days depending on role.
- Marginal cost per 1M tokens served (current blend): $12.40.
- Expected unit savings from quantization/infra tuning (one-off optimization sprint): 8–14% on token cost.

Scenario definitions and triggers:
1) Micro-burst (MB): 15–120 minutes; peak 2–5x baseline.
   - Detection: rolling 30m window >2.5x baseline and sustained 15m.
   - Action: throttle non-critical batch jobs, enable auto-burst credits, no hiring.
   - Pricing lever: short-lived surcharge optional for heavy accounts (>10% of burst).

2) Multi-day spike (MDS): 1–14 days; peak 1.5–2.5x baseline.
   - Detection: 3-day moving average >1.6x baseline OR day-over-day growth >25% for 48h.
   - Action variants: see protocol A/B/C below.

3) Sustained growth (SG): >14 days; net growth baseline+15% sustained.
   - Detection: 14-day rolling avg >1.15x baseline AND projected to persist per product signals.
   - Action: engage hiring pipeline (FTEs), pricing tier adjustments, priority capacity auctions.

Protocol variants (for MDS primarily) — pick one as default, others as alternatives:
- Protocol A: Conservative - "Delay hire, optimize infra"
  - Immediate: deploy infra optimization sprint (deploy KV cache prefixing, raise batching for low-latency-tolerant routes), enable quantization profiles on non-critical models.
  - Threshold to hire contractors: 7-day sustained MDS with >20% margin erosion versus baseline (unit margin < target).
  - Pricing: temporary surcharge band +5–10% on new usage above baseline for >3 days (opt-in for top-tier customers).
  - Headcount action: pull from on-call ops pool; contractor only if optimization yields <10% cost reduction.

- Protocol B: Responsive - "Short-term contractor first" (recommended fallback)
  - Immediate: spin up contractor pool (pre-approved vendors) up to 12-weeks; enable burst capacity reservations.
  - Threshold to hire contractors: 48–72 hours of sustained MDS.
  - Pricing: no immediate surcharge; communicate capacity credits to large customers.
  - Headcount action: hire contractors for SRE/infra shifts and one MLE to run optimization iterations concurrently.

- Protocol C: Aggressive - "Fast FTE" (for strategic segments)
  - Immediate: approve expedited FTE recruit for critical infra roles (requires exec sign-off).
  - Threshold: evidence of conversion-led growth (new paid cohorts driving >15% incremental tokens/week) OR sustained MDS >7 days and forecast shows persistence.
  - Pricing: introduce temporary premium for new accounts and surge-tier customers; long-term customers get credit offsets.

Pricing sensitivity sketches (notes, not final):
- Sensitivity axis: 1) surcharge level (0%, 5%, 10%), 2) duration (3d, 7d, 14d), 3) mitigation effectiveness (infra opt saves 8%, 12%, 16%).
- Example cell interpretation: 5% surcharge for 7d with 12% infra savings yields net margin delta: - expected extra revenue from surcharge minus opportunity cost from churn risk.
- Quick thumb numbers (baseline):
  - If MDS generates incremental 100M tokens/day for 7 days = 700M tokens.
  - At marginal cost $12.40 /1M tokens -> incremental cost = $8.68k.
  - 5% surcharge (applied at $0.02 per 1k tokens equivalent) approximates incremental revenue of $7k over 7d (very coarse).
  - If infra opt reduces cost by 12% -> saved $1.04k; combined with surcharge improves cover but not fully.
  - Hiring a single 12-week contractor (SRE) incremental cost ~ $18k pro-rated for spike window -> generally not economical for <14-day isolated spikes unless slope triggers additional value (retention, conversion).

Decision matrix (high level):
- MB: Protocol A (no hire) + immediate auto-burst.
- MDS short (1–3d): Protocol B preferred; contractors if >48h and margin erosion >8%.
- MDS medium (4–14d): Protocol B + fast infra opt; escalate to C if sustained >7d and revenue signs positive.
- SG: Protocol C (hire FTEs) and consider pricing tier rework for long term.

Operational runbook snippets (templates):
- Auto-runbook steps for MDS detection (ops team):
  1) Alert: 30m rolling > threshold -> Page SRE lead and finance on-call.
  2) Execute infra throttle playbook for non-critical routes.
  3) Open "MDS incident" doc, assign roles: finance lead, ops lead, product liaison.
  4) Run quick cost-run estimate using the spike calculator (link below).
  5) Decide Protocol A/B/C within 4 hours.

- Communication templates:
  - External: short note to affected customers explaining surge, mitigations, and optional surcharge or credits.
  - Internal: one-pager for execs summarizing cost impact, forecast, and proposed headcount action.

Next steps / asks:
- Finance: build a small calculator widget (sheet) to model: incremental tokens, marginal cost, surcharge revenue, contractor cost, and net margin in a single view.
- Eng: validate rough infra opt savings (8–14%) for the most common overflow routes and estimate time-to-impact.
- Talent/People Ops: confirm contractor panel pricing and minimal onboarding time; produce quick-hire contract template.
- Product: flag signals that indicate conversion-led spikes (trial->paid cohorts, marketing campaigns) so we can prefer Protocol C when growth is strategic.

Open questions / unresolved: 
- Legal on surcharge language: what wording avoids regulatory pushback for enterprise customers in EU? (tagging Legal).
- How to reconcile surcharge with committed customers who expect fixed pricing — need credit offsets or exclusion rules.
- Are there pre-approved exec thresholds for expedited FTE hires? Current policy requires VP+ approval; suggest adding a fast-path for infra roles up to 6 months probation.

Appendix (simple formulas and references):
- incremental_cost = (incremental_tokens / 1e6) * marginal_cost_per_1M
- surcharge_revenue_est = incremental_tokens * surcharge_rate_per_token (define in sheet)
- contractor_pro_rated_cost = contractor_weekly_rate * weeks_allocated_during_spike
- reference: CONFLUENCE-9876 (Q2 capacity playbook), JIRA-FIN-4321 (spike detection tickets).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and assumes the spike calculator will standardize scenario math. Please comment if you prefer Protocol B as the default instead of A.
- If we agree on a default, I'll convert the key thresholds into alerting rules for the monitoring team and draft external customer language.

Signed: Marina
